articles.title: NRLW Premiership: Sydney Roosters crush Brisbane Broncos to claim third NRLW title and complete perfect season
articles.summary: Sydney Roosters ruined NRLW great Ali Brigginshaw’s farewell by crushing Brisbane Broncos 30-6 in the Grand Final, with the Tricolours completing a perfect season
articles.body:
The unstoppable Roosters gave legends Corban Baxter and Millie Elliott the perfect send-off with six tries in a first-half blitz at Accor Stadium.

Sydney won all 11 of their regular-season matches before claiming victory on Sunday to complete a perfect season. It's their third premiership in history, following Grand Final victories in 2021 and 2024.

It was also 31 wins from their last 32 games and a second premiership in the past three seasons and redemption for the 'Tricolours' after losing the same match-up in last year's decider.

Brydie Parker (2), Tarryn Aiken, Isabelle Kelly, Jayme Fressard and Amber Hall all crossed the whitewash as the Roosters produced a dominant first-half display.

Parker completed her Grand Final hat-trick before the hour mark to extend Sydney's lead to 30-0.

Jesse Southwell finally got the Broncos on the board after 63 minutes, but the game was already done and dusted, with the Roosters soon celebrating a crushing victory.

Retiring Roosters forward Millie Elliott said: "Everyone knows what that felt like and we definitely used that as motivation all season, not just in this game, all season," she said.

"And we worked so hard, I take my hat off to [head coach John] Strangey and the coaching staff, they really left no stone unturned this year and we wanted to put in a performance like that."

Winning captain Isabelle Kelly said: "I knew that this year we're creating something special, and I think we're building and made that our best game yet. I love you guys and I'm so glad that we get to do this together."

She added: "To Corban and Millie, you guys have been absolutely incredible for this NRLW competition, but mostly for the Roosters the impact that you guys have had on us, Millie, you being a mum, it's just created such a special bond for us to look forward to for many years. And you'll always be a Rooster."

The heavy loss for Brisbane also marked the end of Ali Brigginshaw's stellar career in the women's game, as the veteran bowed out in disappointing fashion.

articles.title: Pasó inadvertido pero es un gesto deportivo top: Ari Sánchez volea a la red tras el passing de Triay cantado "out"
articles.standfirst: La española, en semifinales, tras la correción del VAR no dudó en errar en la siguiente jugada para compensar el error y recibió el apaluso de las rivales y recibió y el público.
articles.summary: La española, en semifinales, tras la correción del VAR no dudó en errar en la siguiente jugada para compensar el error y recibió el apaluso de las rivales y recibió y el público.
articles.body: Pasó inadvertido, pero es uno de los gestos deportivos del año en el pádel y lo ha protagonizado Ari Sánchez en una jugada que recibió el reconocimiento de rivales y público en Rotterdam. Ari Sánchez ha protagonizado el momento más deportivo del Rotterdam P2 de Premier Padel cuando en la segunda semifinal femenina no dudaría en dejar en la red una volea de revés para corregir una decisión que el VAR había evidenciado. En el inicio del primer set y con 3-0 a favor de Sánchez y Ustero, la jugadora española no llegaría al passing de revés de Gemma Triay que sería cantado inicialmente como "out" por el árbitro del partido, el italiano Edoardo Alfonsi. Una pelota muy justa que generaría dudas en las cuatro jugadoras y ante la que las números uno solicitarían la intervención de la sala VAR (con el colegiado portugués Tomás Sabino) y que acabaría dando la razón a Brea y Triay. La jugada, que tendría que ser repetida tal y como está registrado en el reglamento FIP, iba a acabar con el servicio de Ustero y la final volea de Ari Sánchez a la red para hacer subir al marcador el punto que sus rivales se habían ganado en primera instancia. Un gesto de nivel y máxima deportividad de Sánchez (y Ustero) que reconocería el público de Rotterdam al unísono con el aplauso unánime y al que también se sumarían Brea y Triay en forma de agradecimiento.

articles.title: Asian Games 2026: Curtain comes down in Aichi-Nagoya as Doha receives flag for 2030 edition
articles.summary: The 20th Asian Games came to a glittering close on Sunday, bringing down the curtain on more than two weeks of sporting action in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, as
articles.body: The 20th Asian Games came to a glittering close on Sunday, bringing down the curtain on more than two weeks of sporting action in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, as Qatar received the flag for the next edition in Doha in 2030. Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) President Sheikh Joaan bin Hamad Al Thani officially declared the Games closed at Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium, marking the end of a sporting spectacle that celebrated Asia's athletic excellence.Thousands of athletes, officials and spectators gathered for the closing ceremony, which carried the theme 'One Asia'. The proceedings also featured the formal handover to Qatari representatives, with Doha preparing to host the continent's premier multi-sport event four years from now.India's Neeru Dhanda, who enjoyed a memorable campaign with two gold medals and a silver in shooting, carried the national flag at the ceremony, capping a landmark outing for the Indian contingent.India finishes fourth with 85 medalsIndia signed off with 85 medals — 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze — to finish fourth in the overall standings, behind China, Japan and South Korea.The campaign featured significant performances across shooting, athletics, boxing, hockey and other disciplines, underlining India's growing depth across sports. Neeru's outstanding haul was among the highlights, while India's gold-medal-winning hockey campaigns secured qualifications for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics.India's performance also continued a broader trend of consistent medal hauls at recent Asian Games, following the historic 100-medal milestone at Hangzhou 2023. The Aichi-Nagoya edition offered further evidence of the country's expanding presence across the continental sporting landscape, even as the final tally fell short of the previous edition's overall medal count.Doha receives the baton for 2030The closing ceremony formally shifted attention to the next host city, with Doha set to welcome Asia's sporting community in 2030. The handover marked the beginning of preparations for Qatar's second Asian Games, following its hosting of the event in 2006.The Aichi-Nagoya Games featured 469 gold-medal events across a record programme of 43 sports, with around 17,000 athletes and officials participating. Several disciplines, including padel, mixed martial arts, teqball and surfing, made their Asian Games debuts, reflecting the event's evolving sporting landscape.China dominated the standings with 169 gold medals among 341 medals overall, recording its best gold-medal haul at an Asian Games held outside its home territory. Hosts Japan finished second with 83 golds and 269 medals, surpassing their previous gold-medal record at Hiroshima 1994.Sporting brilliance amid organisational challengesDespite the on-field excitement, the Games faced criticism over accommodation and transport arrangements. Organisers opted against building a dedicated athletes' village, instead using hotels, modular accommodation and a cruise ship to house participants.Registration delays, room-allocation problems and unreliable shuttle services affected several delegations, while diplomatic and ceremonial mix-ups added to the difficulties. Attendance was also subdued at several venues, with accessibility issues contributing to disappointing crowds.Nevertheless, the competition produced several remarkable individual performances, led by China's teenage swimming sensation Yu Zidi and seven-gold winner Zhang Zhanshuo, alongside standout displays in athletics and other disciplines.As Aichi-Nagoya handed over the baton to Doha, the Games closed with a celebration of sporting achievement, even as the organisational shortcomings offered important lessons for the next edition.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: David Catarineu: la casualidad que acabó convirtiéndose en una vida dedicada al salvamento
articles.standfirst: Semifinalista en el primer Campeonato de España de Rescate con Moto Acuática que organiza la Federación Española de Salvamento y Socorrismo
articles.summary: Semifinalista en el primer Campeonato de España de Rescate con Moto Acuática que organiza la Federación Española de Salvamento y Socorrismo
articles.body: David Catarineu i Capellas (Barcelona, 1981) quería jugar al baloncesto. Sus padres, sin embargo, pensaron que un entorno acuático podría protegerle mejor de las lesiones. Aquella decisión familiar, aparentemente nimia, terminó marcando el rumbo de su vida. Comenzó practicando natación y salvamento, y con apenas ocho años ya disputó su primer Campeonato de España, en Tarragona. Su evolución deportiva le llevó a abandonar las competiciones escolares y dar el salto a un club federado, el Club Natació Catalunya. Allí, más allá de los resultados, encontró una forma de entender el deporte que conservaría durante toda su trayectoria. De la mano de Gemma Carnero y Jordi Jerez, ya en el CN Banyoles, llegaron algunos de sus mejores resultados. Catarineu acumuló títulos autonómicos y nacionales, fue reconocido como mejor deportista catalán de Salvamento y Socorrismo entre 2004 y 2009, y batió récords de España en 100 metros aletas, 100 metros socorrista y 200 metros súper socorrista. La competición internacional amplió todavía más su trayectoria. Sumó victorias en Francia, Italia, Alemania y Argentina, consiguiendo la medalla de bronce en el Campeonato de Europa de Tylösand, Suecia, en 200 metros Súper Socorrista. Pero compatibilizar los estudios y la vida laboral terminó siendo incompatible con las exigencias del deporte de alto nivel y tuvo que abandonar aquella etapa. Años después encontró otra forma de regresar y en 2013 comenzó a formar a nuevos socorristas como profesor titular del Técnico Deportivo de Grado Medio y Superior en Salvamento y Socorrismo. La experiencia acumulada durante años pasaba así al aula y actualmente es responsable de formación de la Federación Catalana. Desde la Federación participa en el impulso de proyectos destinados a implementar la educación acuática en la sociedad, trasladando a nuevas generaciones todo lo aprendido durante años dentro del salvamento y socorrismo. David lo resume recurriendo al lema de la Organización Mundial de la Salud: "Cualquiera puede ahogarse, a nadie debería sucederle". Esa frase conecta, en cierto modo, todas las etapas de su trayectoria. Primero aprendió a competir en el agua, después representó a España, batió récords nacionales y subió a podios internacionales. Cuando el alto nivel terminó, encontró otra forma de seguir vinculado: formar y contribuir a que el conocimiento llegue también fuera de la competición. Este fin de semana, Catarineu ha quedado semifinalista en el primer Campeonato de España de Rescate con Moto Acuática que organiza la Federación Española de Salvamento y Socorrismo. Una nueva competición espectacular que se celebra dentro del programa de los Juegos del Agua de Melilla impulsados por ADESP, la Asociación del Deporte Español.

articles.title: WWE Money in the Bank 2026 Picks For Both Ladder Matches
articles.summary: WWE Money in the Bank 2026 is quickly taking shape, with both ladder matches featuring a mix of established stars and some of the company's biggest emerging names.
articles.body:
WWE Money in the Bank 2026 is quickly taking shape, with both ladder matches featuring a mix of established stars and some of the company's biggest emerging names.

CM Punk and Penta have joined Bron Breakker, Je'Von Evans, and Trick Williams in the men's match, while Lash Legend is the latest addition to a women's field that includes Roxanne Perez, Sol Ruca, Lola Vice, and Jacy Jayne.

Here are the Superstars with the best chance of climbing the ladder, who could surprise, and which competitors appear to be long shots.

Breakker brings the power, Evans has the spectacular athleticism, and Williams enters as the reigning United States champion. At the same time, Penta and Punk add plenty of experience and star power to the contest.

Penta should be the pick to win the briefcase, as the former World Heavyweight Championship challenger has already been positioned prominently on Raw, and his recent title match against Roman Reigns gives him momentum heading into the ladder match. A report this week named Penta as WWE's reported internal favorite.

Punk is the biggest threat to that prediction, though, as he qualified by defeating Gunther and Finn Bálor on SmackDown, giving him one of the strongest recent wins of anyone in the field.

If WWE wants a major-name briefcase holder who can immediately turn the championship picture upside down, Punk has an obvious path.

The hardest person to envision winning right now is Williams, as he already holds the U.S. title. That doesn't make a Money in the Bank victory impossible, but adding the briefcase would give WWE two major pieces of championship positioning to manage at once.

Breakker and Evans feel more plausible as future winners, especially if WWE wants to use the briefcase to boost one of its younger stars.

Still, Penta has the strongest combination of recent momentum, championship-level positioning and a storyline-friendly reason to carry the briefcase into the next stage of the WWE calendar.

Of the participants in the women's ladder match, Perez is the only performer with previous Money in the Bank experience, while Ruca and Legend are two of WWE's most explosive young athletes.

Perez is the pick to win since she has already established herself as one of the company's most reliable young Superstars, and her previous Money in the Bank experience gives her an edge in the chaos.

The Prodigy also qualified by winning a Triple Threat over Iyo Sky and La Catalina, putting her directly into the six-woman field.

Legend could be the biggest spoiler, as she just defeated Charlotte Flair and Giulia to qualify, and her size and athleticism make her an obvious threat in a match built around climbing ladders and throwing opponents out of the ring.

Ruca is another intriguing option because the ladder match is a natural showcase for her athletic ability.

For many, Jayne feels like the toughest sell as a winner right now. She already carries the Women's United States Championship, and giving her the Money in the Bank briefcase would create an unnecessary situation with two championship-related prizes at the same time.

Vice also has plenty of upside, but she will be entering the match more as a breakout candidate than the obvious favorite.

WWE has several viable options in this match, but Perez currently has the clearest combination of experience, momentum and storyline potential to leave New Orleans with the briefcase.

articles.title: Red Bull’s Verstappen wins rain-delayed Bahrain GP F1 race in Sepang
articles.summary: Championship leader Kimi Antonelli of Mercedes and Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton finish second and third.
articles.body:
Red Bull’s Max Verstappen has finally won his first race of the Formula One season amid chaotic scenes at the Bahrain Grand Prix, which was held in Malaysia an hour and 40 minutes late due to heavy rain.

Verstappen gained the lead on Sunday after an early safety car and led home the Mercedes of championship leader Kimi Antonelli in second and the Ferrari of Lewis Hamilton in third at the Sepang International Circuit.

But there was agony for George Russell, who had to retire from third place in the second Mercedes with five laps to go when his power unit appeared to fail under a late safety car.

Verstappen was the last driver to win in Sepang in 2017 before it was taken off the F1 calendar, and the Dutchman, who had also taken pole, gave Red ‌‌Bull a huge boost despite an early setback when he lost the lead before turn one.

An eventual standing start saw four-time world champion Verstappen start from pole for the first time this season after dominating practice and qualifying.

But he had a slow getaway on intermediate tyres, allowing the Mercedes pair of Antonelli and Russell to pass him easily in the wet early conditions.

A safety car came out when Valtteri Bottas spun into the gravel on lap nine, and most drivers opted for new slick tyres to take advantage of a rapidly drying track.

Verstappen took a lead that he would not relinquish when the safety car ended, swooping past Antonelli and Russell and quickly opening a comfortable gap.

Hamilton started on the front row on dry tyres and quickly slid down the field in the wet conditions.

But the seven-time world champion used all his experience to work his way back through the field for a brilliant podium place as the surface dried out.

His teammate Charles Leclerc was fourth with Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar in fifth.

The Bahrain Grand Prix was raced in Malaysia due to the United States-Israel war on Iran, which has caused disruptions to the international sports calendar.

Formula One moves on to nearby Singapore for a night race and sprint next weekend.

articles.title: Asian Games 2026 MVPs: Meet teenage sensation Yu Zidi and sprint king Puripol Boonson
articles.summary: The Asian Games have found two new superstars.
articles.body: The Asian Games have found two new superstars.China's 13-year-old swimming sensation Yu Zidi and Thailand's 20-year-old sprinting powerhouse Puripol Boonson were named the Female and Male Most Valuable Players of the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games by the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) on Sunday.The pair were rewarded for spectacular campaigns in which they combined multiple gold medals with a string of Asian Games and Asian records, emerging as two of the brightest young stars of the continental showpiece.Yu and Boonson will each receive USD 25,000 from the OCA for their performances.Yu Zidi: Teen sensation makes historyYu was one of the breakout stars of Aichi-Nagoya, winning three individual gold medals at just 13 years of age and becoming the youngest MVP in Asian Games history.Her golden run began in the women's 200m butterfly, where she clocked 2:05.08 on September 20 to set a new Games Record.A day later, she produced an even more impressive performance in the women's 200m individual medley. Her time of 2:06.10 set a new Games Record and lowered the Asian Record.Yu completed her hat-trick on September 23, winning the women's 400m individual medley in 4:28.56, another Games Record.Three events, three golds and four records made the Chinese teenager one of the defining faces of the Games.Boonson: Thailand's sprint kingIf Yu ruled the pool, Boonson owned the track.The 20-year-old Thai sprinter stormed to a 100m-200m double, setting four Asian Games Records and equalling an Asian Record during his campaign.In the men's 100m, Boonson first broke the Games Record with 9.91 seconds in the semifinal before going even faster in the final, clocking 9.90 seconds to claim gold on September 25.Two days later, he completed the sprint double in the 200m. His winning time of 19.88 seconds broke his own Games Record of 20.10 seconds and equalled the Asian Record.He also added a silver medal in Thailand's mixed 4x100m relay, further underlining his impact in Aichi-Nagoya.Stars with Los Angeles in sightThe OCA MVP Awards Panel said the selection was particularly difficult because of the exceptional quality of performances across the Games.Tayyab Ikram, chair of the five-member panel, said Yu and Boonson had established themselves as "Asian sports superstars" and backed them to achieve even greater success at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics.Their selection places them alongside a distinguished list of previous Asian Games MVPs, including Japan's Koji Ito and Kosuke Kitajima, China's Lin Dan and Rikako Ikee, and the 2022 winners Qin Haiyang and Zhang Yufei.For Yu, still only 13, and Boonson, at 20, Aichi-Nagoya could prove to be only the beginning. articles.title: Asian Games: Leaner Indian contingent produces fewer golds but better return-per-medal - in numbers
articles.summary: In late August, the Sports Ministry maintained that the qualification criteria for the Asian Games, put into place a year ago, would not change despite
articles.body: In late August, the Sports Ministry maintained that the qualification criteria for the Asian Games, put into place a year ago, would not change despite criticism. “The idea, from the very beginning, was to send a lean contingent. The criteria was announced a year ago, and everyone had the time to figure it out and qualify,” a Sports Ministry source told TimesofIndia.com back then. It was made clear that the objective was to have a contingent with only realistic medal contenders making the trip to Aichi-Nagoya."Let’s take an example. If somebody has to run inside 10 seconds to be a contender for a medal in the 100m event, should we send an athlete who clocks 15 seconds? We have set the criteria that if an athlete is in the top six in Asia, we will select him or her, otherwise not. We have followed that,” the source had said.The tennis squad went from 12 to 7. Several judokas and wushu athletes were removed from the initial list. From 44 players in 2022, no footballers were sent this time. There was also no place for 20 hoopers and 16 handball players.India had sent a 661-athlete contingent to the 2022 Asian Games in Hangzhou. Three years later, the final contingent that travelled to Japan was trimmed to 495 athletes. After 14 days of competition, India accounted for 21 golds, 27 silvers and 37 bronzes for a combined 85 medals. For comparison, India had won 106 medals in China (28 golds, 38 silvers, and 40 bronze).As the contingent size dropped by 25.1%, the golds fell by nearly the same number (25%) and medals by 19.8%. India won 16 medals for every 100 athletes in Hangzhou. In Aichi-Nagoya, that figure rose to 17.2% — an improvement of about 7.3%.Stripped to the bare bones, India won 0.172 medals per athlete in Nagoya, against 0.160 in Hangzhou. Golds per athlete were essentially unchanged at about 0.042. Crudely, it counts every athlete sent, including those who did not medal. At the same time, teams as big as cricket (30 athletes), hockey (40) and kabaddi (24) account for a single medal in a discipline.So while India did not match its record 106-medal haul, its smaller contingent produced a slightly better medal return per athlete.The more complicated part of the comparison comes when gold medals are brought into the mix.India's gold medal tally fell from 28 to 21, a 25% decline — exactly in line with the reduction in the size of the contingent. The gold-medal yield was therefore virtually unchanged: 4.24 golds per 100 athletes in Hangzhou and 4.24 in Aichi-Nagoya.That suggests the smaller contingent was not, by itself, the reason India's gold tally fell. Rather, the composition of the medal haul changed.Where did the golds go?India's 2022 golds came heavily from three sports: shooting (seven), athletics (six), and archery (five), which is 18 of 28 (64%). In Nagoya, archery again delivered five, but shooting produced three and athletics one. Boxing, which won no gold in Hangzhou, won three, and wrestling won two after none. Golf added a gold courtesy Pranavi Urs. Squash, which won two golds in 2022, won none, despite the expectations from Anahat Singh, though the overall count of five medals did not change.The team sports carried more of the load. Cricket, hockey and kabaddi won six of India's 21 golds, up from five of 28. India completed a double title finish in all three. In 2022, hockey had produced one gold and one bronze.Athletics' podium shifted down a step. In 2022, it returned six golds, 14 silvers and nine bronzes. Now, despite a massive 75-plus-member contingent, it produced one gold, nine silvers and 14 bronzes.Shooting, athletics behind the declineShooting (4) and athletics (5) were the biggest reasons behind the drop in gold medals. Squash (2), Badminton (1), Tennis (1) and Equestrian (1) all also witnessed a drop in the yellow metal. Tennis, in fact, didn't produce a medal at all - a first in 40 years.In Hangzhou, shooting and athletics were the two biggest contributors to India's gold medal tally, producing seven and six gold medals, respectively. Together, they accounted for 13 of India's 28 golds. In Aichi-Nagoya, that combined figure collapsed to four. Shooting contributed three golds, while athletics produced one. India therefore lost nine gold medals from these two sports alone.The sub-par show from the athletes was made murkier by the withdrawals of 100m hurdler Jyothi Yarraji and triple jumper Praveen Chithravel. Both national record holders had skipped the Indian Athletics Series Final in prelude to the Asian Games, citing knee stress and a calf muscle pull, respectively.When it came to the Asian Games, Yarraji pulled out of the women's 100m hurdles first-round heats after "feeling pain" during the warm-up under rainy conditions.Chithravel, meanwhile, attempted his first jump but could not complete it, exiting the competition area clutching his calf in apparent pain. He was later taken away in a wheelchair. Men's 400m hurdler Yashas P., too, pulled out after starting his Heat.Coming to the shooters.India's 2026 shooting tally of 15 medals (3 golds, 8 silvers and 4 bronzes) was a 32% drop in total medal tally when compared to 22 in the previous continental showpiece. The gold haul took a 57% hit. Broken further, seven were team medals, five individual and three in mixed team events.The gold medals came in one individual (Neeru Dhanda in women's trap) and two mixed team events (Neeru and Kynan Chenai in mixed trap and Suruchi Phogat and Kamaljeet in mixed 10m air pistol).Late surge takes India to 85 medals and fourth spotIf the final medal tally tells one story, the daily trajectory tells another. Through the first 12 days of competition, India had won 10 gold medals in Aichi-Nagoya. In Hangzhou, India had already accumulated 21 golds by the same point.Then came the late surge in Japan.India won 11 gold medals over the final two days of its 2026 campaign — six on Day 13 and five on Day 14. That means 52.4% of India's entire gold haul came in the final two days. The equivalent figure in Hangzhou was 25%: seven of India's 28 golds came during the final two days.India had 13 golds by Day 8 in Hangzhou. At the same stage in Aichi-Nagoya, it had four. By Day 11, the gap was still eight golds — 18 to 10.But the final stretch changed the picture dramatically. India collected 18 golds across Days 13 and 14 in the two editions combined, but the distribution was very different: seven in Hangzhou and 11 in Aichi-Nagoya.On October 2, the women's recurve team of Ankita Bhakat, Kirti Sharma and Kumkum Mohod picked a gold. As did boxer Lovlina Borgohain on her birthday. Parveen Hooda also joined the party alongside wrestler Sujeet Kalkal's remarkable comeback, boxer Ankush Panghal's drought-ending gold, and the women's hockey team's triumph over China to seal an LA 2028 spot.A day later, archer Kumkum Mohod, golfer Pranavi Urs, wrestler Aman Sehrawat, the men's cricket team, and the men's hockey team gave the country plenty to celebrate with golden flourishes.The overall medal gap never disappearedThe same late surge was visible in the total medal count, but it was not enough to close the gap with Hangzhou.After the first day, India had five medals in Hangzhou and two in Aichi-Nagoya.By Day 4, the difference had grown to 10 medals.By Day 8, it was 16.By Day 11, Hangzhou's cumulative tally stood at 80 medals, compared with 60 in Aichi-Nagoya — a 20-medal gap.India narrowed that deficit slightly over the next two days, reaching 76 medals against Hangzhou's 94 after Day 13.But the final day added nine medals in Aichi-Nagoya and 12 in Hangzhou, leaving the final difference to 21.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Amid teen triumph and organisational chaos, Asian Games close in Japan
articles.summary: The continental competition hosted 17,000 athletes over two weeks in Aichi-Nagoya.
articles.body:
After two weeks of youthful brilliance on the field amid logistical dysfunction and subdued public interest off it, the curtain has come down on the 20th Asian Games in Japan.

Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) president Sheikh Joaan bin Hamad Al Thani declared the Games closed at Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium on Sunday, with the torch handed to organisers of the next event in Doha, Qatar, in 2030.

Some 17,000 athletes and officials came for the Aichi-Nagoya showpiece – more than the participants in the Paris Olympics – with athletes competing in 469 gold-medal events spanning Tokyo to Osaka.

The massive scale clashed with organisers’ planning for a “simple, streamlined and functional event” — and the results were often chaotic.

Athletes and teams complained of bungled accommodation and transport, prompting repeated apologies from the embarrassed organising committee.

Despite the challenges, the games were lifted by the performances of teenage titans, led by China’s 13-year-old swimmer Yu Zidi .

Awarded the female Most Valuable Player (MVP) of the games, Yu is on track for a huge Los Angeles Olympics after claiming three individual gold medals in the Tokyo pool.

She swam the second-fastest time in winning the 200 metres individual medley, setting up a battle royale with Canada’s world-record holder Summer McIntosh.

Her 19-year-old teammate Zhang Zhanshuo became the first swimmer to win seven golds at the games, while Japan’s 17-year-old wunderkind Shin Ohashi smashed the 200m breaststroke world record.

Track and field events were lit up by young athletes as well, with China’s 18-year-old Yan Ziyi producing a world-class throw to win the women’s javelin gold while 20-year-old Thai sprinter Puripol Boonson swept the 100m and 200m to become the men’s MVP.

The athletes performed despite regular logistical failures and occasional diplomatic gaffes.

“Accommodation, transport and other issues — it seems a lot of teams were affected,” Hong Kong team chef de mission Wong Po-kee told the Reuters news agency on Sunday.

Organisers opted to house athletes and officials in a mix of hotels, wooden container units and a cruise ship to cut costs rather than build a dedicated athletes’ village.

They budgeted for 15,000 athletes and officials — about 2,000 fewer than total registrations — and struggled to manage them.

Waves of athletes spent up to 12 hours waiting to be registered on arrival.

While checking in, some found their rooms double-booked or being shared by the wrong teammates.

Transport problems dogged the games throughout, with athletes’ shuttle buses failing to turn up or taking them to the wrong venues . Several competitions were delayed due to these errors.

South Korea’s delegation was particularly aggrieved, with their team chef de mission marking the games’ organisation with an “F”, the lowest grade.

South Korean men’s footballers were upset when their national flag could not be hoisted for the national anthem at the victory ceremony after they beat Japan for the gold medal on Saturday.

Earlier, the North Korean national anthem was played for South Korea’s men’s hockey team in another awkward mix-up.

Five years after the Tokyo Olympics were staged without fans due to COVID-19 restrictions, Japan’s first major multisport event was blighted by poor crowds.

Fewer than 1,000 spectators watched the hosts beat South Korea in a women’s football semifinal at a 50,000-capacity stadium.

Much smaller venues were often nearly empty, though many were based in far-flung locations, making access a challenge.

“If I had to say, well, I don’t think it was a success,” Nagoya resident Naoko Toda, who watched several competitions, told Reuters before the closing ceremony.

Despite the issues, the games’ governing body OCA declared Aichi-Nagoya a success and praised organisers for their frugal arrangements.

China topped the table with 341 medals, including 169 gold, with its best haul at an overseas Asian Games.

Japan also delivered for fans who tuned in, with 83 gold medals out of 269, smashing its previous record at Hiroshima 1994.

Padel, mixed martial arts, teqball and surfing made their games debuts in a record 43-sport programme that dwarfed the Paris Olympics.

Qatar is set to host the next continental games in 2030, though the OCA may elect to push it back a year to serve as the continent’s Olympic qualifiers before Brisbane 2032.

articles.title: WRC: Elfyn Evans becomes world champion after late Oliver Solberg crash
articles.summary: Five-time runner-up Elfyn Evans is world champion for the first time after rival Oliver Solberg crashes in the final moments of Rally Italia Sardegna.
articles.body:
Five-time runner-up Elfyn Evans is world champion for the first time after rival Oliver Solberg crashed in a dramatic finish to the Rally Italia Sardegna.

Sweden's Solberg was on course to snatch the lead on the final stage of the last round of the World Rally Championship (WRC) when he crashed with less than 100 metres to go.

"It hasn't sunk in," said a shocked Evans, who became the first British world champion in 25 years.

"I was sure it was over. I feel for Oliver, he had an incredible weekend. I don't know what to say."

The 37-year-old and co-driver Scott Martin had led for much of the 2026 season and took a 21-point advantage into the final round in Sardinia.

But that gap had shrunk to a solitary point by the time the drivers lined up for the last of 17 stages, bringing back painful memories of previous narrow misses for Evans.

Solberg, 25, needed only to beat his Toyota team-mate in the final stage to claim enough bonuses to be champion, but crashed two corners from the finish.

Evans becomes only the third British man to win the WRC title after Colin McRae in 1995 and Richard Burns in 2001.

Relive dramatic final stage shootout for title as it happened

The five titles that got away as Evans seeks WRC glory

Solberg, whose father Petter won the WRC title in 2003, won the rally by almost a minute ahead of nine-time world champion Sebastien Ogier.

He and English co-driver Elliott Edmondson were also on course to win the final stage and collect a maximum 35 points for the weekend to take the title by two points.

However, his crash meant he finished five points behind Evans in the overall standings.

A third Toyota driver, Sami Pajari, finished a further one point behind in third - having seen his own title challenge evaporate on the final weekend.

An inconsolable Solberg remained in his car for some time at the end of the stage before being encouraged to take to the podium by Gazoo Racing team principal Jari-Matti Latvala and team-mate Ogier.

"Two corners, two corners," said an emotional Solberg.

"First congratulations to Elfyn, he has been very consistent all season. That I even had a shot after my rollercoaster of a season is incredible.

"I tried everything. I knew I was pushing but didn't know if it was enough. I pushed even more and I couldn't save the car. I tried my very best."

Evans, from Dolgellau in north Wales, had previously missed out on the title on the final day three times and in two of those seasons he had taken a lead into the concluding rally before losing out to Ogier in 2020 and 2025.

"I don't really know what my reaction is. It's surreal with how it happened. It's a relief," he said.

"It wouldn't by my proudest way of winning it, but it's job done."

For Toyota sporting director Kaj Lindstrom there were mixed feelings.

"That was the hardest thing. The ending was quite something, I didn't expect it," said the Finn.

"It was a good fight and we all saw that Oliver was all or nothing. It held all the way to the end.

"Oliver still has time but Elfyn finally got his title so we're really happy for him."

The WRC season was reduced to 13 rounds when the Saudi Arabia event, originally planned for next month, was cancelled because of the ongoing unrest in the Middle East.

Rally Italia Sardegna marked the end of Jon Armstrong's rookie season at the top level of WRC, and he produced his best result when finishing seventh.

"It's been good to have a clean weekend with a strong result," said the M-Sport Ford driver.

"It's not been an easy year and this was a rally to show we can put it together. A big thanks to everyone who has been supporting us, it's been a great year and it's been a privilege to drive this car."

Armstrong's team-mate and fellow Irishman Josh McErlean did not fare as well despite running as high as sixth on Saturday before retiring after a collision with a tree.

He also had to stop twice on Sunday before finishing well off the pace but claimed ninth spot in the championship.

articles.title: P.J. Fleck can't escape criticism even after Minnesota beats Michigan
articles.summary: Fleck is getting criticized after he didn't have the Gophers attempt a two-point conversion after the go-ahead touchdown in the fourth quarter.
articles.body:
Even on one of the best days of his life , Gophers head coach P.J. Fleck can't avoid criticism.

After Saturday's 20-14 victory to reclaim the Little Brown Jug , Fleck found himself having to explain why he didn't have the Gophers attempt a two-point conversion after Drake Lindsey connected with Darius Taylor for a three-yard touchdown early in the fourth quarter.

Minnesota kicked the extra point to take a 20-14 lead with 13:44 left in the game. Going for two made sense because a successful conversion would've given the Gophers a 21-14 lead. For Fleck, it was too early to go for two.

"I don't chase points. If anybody knows me, this isn't a secret. Here I'm giving you inside what I think. Jim Tressel taught me a long time ago: never chase points. I never go for two until the fourth quarter. Period," Fleck explained.

"We were so close to the beginning of the fourth quarter, though, that if we kicked it, it made it a six-point game. Let's say they went down and scored a touchdown. Well, we're still within that range. Or, if we get the ball back and they don't score, we can go down and kick a field goal and be up two scores. If we don't get [the two-point conversion], then it's a different deal. So just take the points."

After kicking the extra point to take a six-point lead, they indeed could've stopped Michigan and kicked a field goal to increase the lead to nine points, making it a two-score game. Had they gone for two and failed, their lead would've been five points, and another field goal would've kept Michigan within eight points.

On the flip side, not going for two risked allowing Michigan to take the lead with a touchdown and an extra point. That's where Fleck's confidence in how the game was going comes into play. Minnesota's defense completely dominated the Wolverines.

"The best decision, because it was so close to the beginning of the fourth quarter, in my opinion, based on how the game was flowing, take the one, man. It wasn't even a thought in my head. We had talked about it, and I was like, 'No, no, no.' Don't chase points. Too early to chase points," Fleck said.

At one point, from 11:18 left in the second quarter until 14:51 left in the fourth quarter, Michigan had run nine plays for zero total yards. The two touchdowns Michigan scored were after interceptions by Lindsey. The first interception gave Michigan the ball at the Minnesota 34-yard line, and the second was returned 76 yards for a touchdown.

Other than that, Michigan never moved the ball deeper than Minnesota's 39-yard line.

The best decision, because it was so close to the beginning of the fourth quarter, in my opinion, based on how the game was flowing, take the one, man. It wasn't even a thought in my head. We had talked about it and I was like, 'No, no no.' Don't chase points. Too early to chase points."

articles.title: Winners and losers from F1's bug-ridden Bahrain GP in Malaysia
articles.summary: Who can leave Malaysia happy and who will be frustrated?
articles.body:
On a day Formula 1 didn't cover itself in glory with its complicated set of 2026 regulations, the Malaysia edition of the Bahrain Grand Prix still delivered an absorbing race with a few standout performers.

F1's one-off event in Sepang was marred from the start by significant logistical issues affecting spectators. And while those improved as the weekend went on, the on-track spectacle was also not without a hitch as the season's first wet-weather race was plagued by software issues. Such is life in F1 2026.

That's a shame, because pound for pound Sepang is one of the best circuits gracing the calendar. But regardless of power unit gremlins, weather and safety cars, the right man and team still won, writing history with a first-every victory for a brand-new power unit manufacturer.

Max Verstappen has racked up a few special wins in his 10-year stint as a frontline contender, but there were a few reasons why number 72 - good lord - was extra special.

There was a feeling that last weekend's Azerbaijan Grand Prix was going to be Red Bull's best opportunity to get off the mark this year, ahead of Mercedes much-anticipated car upgrade in Malaysia, only for Red Bull to do "a great job messing it up" as Verstappen had to settle for second.

But with Mercedes much less competitive than expected, it was really Red Bull's own progress that stole the headlines, unleashing the real performance gains of its Azerbaijan upgrade on the swoops of Sepang, which the lower downforce Baku street circuit had perhaps kept under wraps.

Verstappen's dominant pole-to-flag win in Malaysia wasn't as straightforward as it really should have been, thanks to the FIA's crippling software issues, the changing weather conditions and a safety car, but it ended the chance of him enduring a winless season.

October 4 was not just a momentous day for Verstappen, though. Verstappen's 72th win was also the first for Red Bull Ford Powertrains as a power unit manufacturer. Coming after Verstappen extended his Red Bull contract until 2030, albeit with the usual exit clauses, the Malaysian weekend saw his faith in the project rewarded.

It is a feather in the cap of the 700-plus staff at the RBPT in Milton Keynes, its colleagues at Ford and also former Red Bull F1 chief Christian Horner, who was the driving force behind Red Bull spreading its wings as a bona fide manufacturer.

Mercedes' visit to the home of its title sponsor Petronas can only be described as a huge disappointment. The performance of its upgraded W17 fell flat, perhaps because of the uniquely difficult conditions on the rough and hot Sepang tarmac, while the team appears to also have made its car more draggy on the straights as a logical result of the downforce increase.

"We don't really know if it made us go faster or worse," said Kimi Antonelli after finishing third. It is perfectly possible that Malaysia is a one-off, with next weekend's Singapore Grand Prix perhaps offering more clues on the real potential of Mercedes' newest spec.

What is harder for the team to accept is the latest reliability issue with its power unit as George Russell's engine expired shortly before the end of the race, not only costing the Briton a podium but arresting the momentum of his Baku victory as his title chances further slip away.

Just a handful of laps into the race, Lewis Hamilton looked down and out as his team's gamble for slicks on a wet but only slowly drying track didn't pan out. "As we pulled out [of the pits], all the spray came out the back of Max's car and I was like: 'Okay, I'm done. My race is really in trouble.'

Falling over a pitstop behind in a matter of two laps, Hamilton felt he had no choice to commit to his soft tyres. But once slicks were the right tyre to be on, the seven-time world champion was rapid as he moved up the order, helped by a safety car reset to get rid of the medium tyres he wasn't a big fan of.

"For us to get back to the podium, I never thought that that was going to be the case," said Hamilton, though he pointed out his disagreement with the squad's tyre gamble at the start would have to be discussed further. "I'm not going to go to the casino with the guys," he jested.

Mercedes isn't the only team heading to Singapore in a state of confusion. McLaren's outstanding pace on high downforce circuits like Budapest, Zandvoort or Madrid appears to have vanished despite the team having recently upgraded its car, too.

"The picture changed very rapidly," Stella acknowledged as we quizzed him about his team's regression. "We have to take a look at our own development. We don't see any anomaly in our data. But we have to acknowledge that potentially some competitors have developed their car with bigger steps than we did. It's a very specific condition here in Malaysia, so I think we should give ourselves more time."

That general lack of competitiveness was compounded on Lando Norris' side of the garage by recurring power unit issues which left the reigning world champion short on straight-line speed.

If anything, McLaren's general lack of performance made the squad's decision to start both cars on slicks less punishing. Oscar Piastri roughly finished where he deserved to be in sixth, with Norris set to shadow the Australian until he had to take avoiding action under the late safety car and dropped back a number of places.

Like Ferrari and others, Stella explained McLaren was caught out by how slowly the circuit was drying out despite the hot conditions. "On this kind of tarmac the intermediate tyres were getting damaged very, very rapidly and the dry tyres worked much more easily than pretty much every other circuit. But as a matter of fact, it took more laps than we thought."

Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing, Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls

Racing Bulls made a tricky race look relatively straightforward. That's what you get when you pair a quick car with solid driving and correct strategy calls as Liam Lawson proved the pick of the bunch in F1's midfield.

Lawson is doing everything the squad can ask of him, but still isn't guaranteed a drive for next year as the team nears a decision between the New Zealander and F2 star Nikola Tsolov. A weekend like Malaysia certainly won't hurt his chances.

In the other car Arvid Lindblad also produced a commendable display as he overcame an engine penalty to take a final point, passing Nico Hulkenberg on the final lap of the race. "We definitely got the basics right today," said team boss Alan Permane.

Several midfield teams endured a frustrating afternoon, including Haas and Williams. But perhaps none more so than Audi, which was on the cusp of a point until Hulkenberg got picked off by Lindblad on the final lap.

Actually, the German could have gone on to greater things if it hadn't been for the safety car, which undid his correct timing to move to the slick tyres.

"Man, I was eating my steering wheel in that moment," Hulkenberg recounted. "Seriously, that sucked. I was feeling brave and like a hero in that moment, and made it work quite well. I think we could have undercut a few people there, but unfortunately, the safety car had other plans."

Gabriel Bortoleto also didn't have the most auspicious of afternoons after taking out Carlos Sainz, netting him a 10-second penalty. Bortoleto initially blamed the Williams driver for not leaving him enough room, but swiftly changed his mind after watching the replay.

"It was a bit frustrating to be overtaking in the last lap again, because that's two races consecutively where we've been done in the last lap," racing director Allan McNish summed up. "And that's a little bit frustrating.

It has taken a particular set of circumstances for Fernando Alonso and Aston Martin to find their way into the points for a third time this season. But while the team's Honda engine deficit was brutally exposed in Baku, a more balanced layout in Kuala Lumpur showcased the team's strides on the chassis side.

No thanks to the team's call to start on slicks, which necessitated the mid-race safety car to get Alonso back into the picture. But other than that error, which was made by over half of the grid, Aston grabbed its chance with aplomb. "There are not many weekends where we can score points and in those weekends we cannot have any mistakes," Alonso said. "We cannot lose the opportunity, so we executed well today, so I'm happy for the team, for the points.

With what should be an even better Aston circuit coming up in the streets of Singapore, the Malaysia performance even gave the wily Spanish veteran a spring in his step again. "Yeah, absolutely. I think Singapore on paper is better than Malaysia, so it's encouraging for next weekend. It's going to be an exciting next five days, waiting for the first qualifying session."

articles.title: Recruiting Roundup: Husky Commit Gets All-American Bowl Invite
articles.summary: Happy Sunday Husky fans. After another tough outing for our Huskies the team will return home this weekend looking to rebound against a tough Iowa team. Ther...
articles.body:
Happy Sunday Husky fans. After another tough outing for our Huskies the team will return home this weekend looking to rebound against a tough Iowa team. There will likely be handful of visitors on campus but with the game being Friday I would bet the recruits in attendance will be a little light.

4 star QB commit Blake Roskopf from Desert Edge HS, AZ got an invitation to the Navy All-American bowl, which is a pretty prestigious honor as most recruiting junkies know. Roskopf, who should have a chance to battle for playing time next year, has thrown for 1,748 yards and 18 touchdowns (versus 6 int's). Listed at 6'6" and around 225 pounds Roskopf has ideal size for the next level and has enough mobility that he can move the chains when needed. Husky fans should be extremely excited for Roskopf to head to Montlake.

We didn't discuss this last weekend, but the Huskies just missed out on Roskopf's 2028 teammate, 4 star edge Jalanie George. The Huskies were leading for a long time for George and it looked like a commitment was imminent, however a recent visit to Wisconsin and large NIL offer from them ended up swaying him to Madison and the Huskies remain without a 2028 commit. I wouldn't worry about not having a commit yet in the 2028 class as it's still early, but the Huskies need to start winning more battles for players like George if they want to continue to move up to the upper echelons of the B1G. We should start to see some additions at the end of the year for the Huskies for their 2028 class.

That is all for today and as always follow me @asieverkropp.

articles.title: UCF linebacker announces return after eligibility fight
articles.summary: Cole Kozlowski announced his UCF Knights return after two months of legal limbo. The fifth-year linebacker transferred from Colgate in 2025.
articles.body:
At long last, Cole Kozlowski will rejoin the UCF football team.

The fifth-year linebacker announced in a social media post on Oct. 4 that he has officially received extra eligibility.

"Everything happens for a reason!" Kozlowski wrote on X. "After recent ruling, I have now been granted eligibility for the rest of the 2026-27 football season. Unbelievably blessed for the opportunity to strap up the helmet and play the game I've loved since I was 5 years old."

Kozlowski enrolled in classes in August and has remained around the team following a July 31 injunction in the U.S. District Court of Colorado that gave an extra season to all Class of 2022 high school graduates.

However, an Aug. 21 ruling in the Tenth Circuit Court of Appeals put that on hold. Kozlowski sat in limbo.

He thanked McCarter & English law firm in his post.

Kozlowski spent the first three seasons of his college career at Colgate. He transferred to UCF before the 2025 campaign and started nine of the Knights ' 12 games. He ranked second on the squad with 82 tackles while also contributing two sacks and forcing a fumble.

"He just kept getting better and better and better and better," UCF linebackers coach Mark D'Onofrio told the News-Journal in August. "He's got a really good knack for the football. He really loves Saturdays."

O'Connell shared , "He's going to get treatment throughout the next couple of days and the goal is try to get him back out there practicing next week. I know it's a big one for him next week going to Louisiana."

In his absence in Week 4, Jordan Addison is expected to step up as the team's WR1. The former first-round pick could be a WR1 on a lot of other teams, so in Jefferson's absence, he will have a chance to showcase himself. In Week 3, he racked up five receptions for 90 yards and one score.

articles.title: Mike Norvell has a 'path' to saving his job at FSU
articles.summary: Mike Norvell is still on the hot seat, but after FSU's win over Virginia, 247Sports believes there is a path for him to save his job.
articles.body:
The FSU Seminoles beat the Virginia Cavaliers on Saturday, routing them 38-7 in Doak Campbell Stadium. The win has them 3-2 on the season and 1-1 in ACC play.

It was a massive win for Mike Norvell, who entered the weekend with arguably the hottest seat in the country. And while one win over an unranked Virginia is not enough for him to save his job, Chris Hummer of 247Sports does believe that Norvell "has a path to potentially save his job."

Hummer believes Norvell can "change his fate" and mentioned FSU's upcoming three-game stretch against the Louisville Cardinals , Miami Hurricanes, and Clemson Tigers. Miami still looks like a juggernaut, but the games against Louisville and Clemson look much more winnable after both teams lost last week.

Some other factors could help out Norvell, who has a 41-36 record as FSU's head coach. The Seminoles do not currently have an athletic director after firing Michael Alford, and would owe Norvell a massive buyout should they fire him. He is due 85% of his remaining contract, and it is believed they would owe him over $40 million should they move on from him this year.

The next step for FSU is building off the momentum they created on Saturday, something they have struggled to do over the past two seasons. They have not won back-to-back games against a Power Four opponents since the 2023 season.

articles.title: Jordan's Review: Mistakes cost Auburn on Rocky Top | OPINION
articles.summary: Phillip Jordan points out the critical mistakes Auburn made in its SEC loss to No. 17 Tennessee on Saturday.
articles.body:
The Auburn Tigers had chances to get a victory over the Tennessee Volunteers on Saturday, but some familiar issues returned in Knoxville. Auburn lost 24-14 in a game they needed to win with the upcoming schedule and dropped to 3-2 on the season with a 1-2 SEC record.

The biggest culprit in the Tigers' loss on Saturday night was mistakes. These missteps were not isolated to just one area or position group. The offensive line, though, is a good place to start. It was once again a rough outing for a group that has struggled in the first five games of the season. They committed six false starts that resulted in putting the offense behind the chains.

It started on the Tigers' first drive of the game.

After Auburn forced Tennessee to punt after five plays, the Tigers got the ball at their own 9-yard line. When looking at a manageable 3rd and 3, Stanton Ramil moved early and made it 3rd and 8. The Tigers did not pick up the first down and had to punt. The trend continued throughout the afternoon and early evening. The way the drive started was also a trend that led to being defeated by the Volunteers. Three times in the game, punt returner Bryce Cain made a fair catch inside the Auburn 10-yard line. The correct approach would be to let the ball bounce; otherwise, it could result in a touchback.

Turnovers were a problem too. Byrum Brown committed three turnovers: two interceptions and one fumble. The fumble in the second quarter was basically canceled out due to Tennessee fumbling the ball back to Auburn four plays later. The big one was the first interception thrown in the second half. With 5:25 remaining in the third, Brown overthrew a pass that was picked off by Dejuan Lane and returned for 32 yards. The second interception ended any hopes of a victory with 0:51 remaining.

It was not just the players; the coaches also made mistakes in the game. The biggest mishap was the decision on 4th down and 1 from the Auburn 24-yard line with 6:34 remaining. It is not the decision to attempt the fourth-down conversion, but the play that was called. Instead of attempting a quarterback sneak with Brown, Auburn ran a pitch to Jeremiah Cobb, who fell short of the first down. The Volunteers followed that up by adding another score to go up 24-14 when running back Desean Bishop scored on a five-yard touchdown with 3:30 remaining in the game.

Going for the 1st down made sense with Auburn having momentum at that point in the game. Auburn had just scored a touchdown on their prior possession to make the game 17-14 when Brown found Arlis Boardingham on a 16-yard jump pass that was set up by a 57-yard run by Brown one play prior.

This does not go into the mistake category, but the Tigers again had issues stopping the run game. The Volunteers rushed for 237 yards and were led by Bishop for 220 yards and three touchdowns. For Auburn, they did rush for 186 yards, but 107 of those were from Brown. Cobb was limited in the game for 17 yards on three carries, but Omar Mabson proved why he should get more carries. He had 62 yards on ten attempts.

Auburn will take an off week after this defeat and will next play at Georgia on Oct. 17. Alex Golesh and his coaching staff will need to regroup to get this season back on track. The mistakes made against Tennessee can be corrected, but if they are not, more losses are in the future of the 2026 Auburn Tigers.

articles.summary: LONDON (AP) — Commanders quarterback Marcus Mariota went to the locker room to have his knee evaluated after a sack in the first quarter of Washington's game...
articles.body:
LONDON (AP) — Commanders quarterback Marcus Mariota went to the locker room to have his knee evaluated after a sack in the first quarter of Washington's game against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday.

Washington is already without starter Jayden Daniels , who had been ruled out Friday because of an elbow injury, so third-stringer Athan Kaliakmanis was called into action.

Mariota was listed as questionable to return. He hadn't come back by halftime, when Indianapolis led 10-6.

With the Commanders ahead 3-0, Mariota was sacked at the Indy 11 by Adetomiwa Adebawore and Laiatu Latu on third down. Mariota walked gingerly to the sideline, and Drew Stevens kicked a field goal for a 6-0 lead.

That drive started with a Mariota keeper around the left end that went for 35 yards.

Kaliakmanis completed six of 12 passes for 33 yards by halftime.

The Commanders selected Kaliakmanis out of Rutgers in the seventh round of the 2026 NFL draft.

The team's website notes that Kaliakmanis is a proud Greek-American : "Kaliakmanis' family is Greek, and he wears his heritage with pride. He has a tattoo sleeve on his left arm with the word οικογένεια, which means family, and another icon representing Saint Athanasius of Alexandria, whom (he) is named after."

Among Kaliakmanis' nicknames: "The Greek Rifle."

articles.title: Daryz claims rare back-to-back success in the Arc
articles.summary: Daryz repeats last year's success in the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe, becoming just the ninth horse to win Europe's richest Flat race more than once.
articles.body:
Daryz became just the ninth horse to win the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe for a second time, repeating his 2025 success with a late burst to claim victory in the richest Flat race in Europe.

The Francis-Henri Graffard trained four-year-old became the first colt to double up in the Arc at ParisLongchamp since Alleged did it 48 years ago.

Mickael Barzalona, the winning jockey last year, took the ride again and expertly manoeuvred Daryz through the 16-strong field to hit the front in the closing stages.

The 13-8 favourite needed a photo finish last year but this time claimed victory by more than a length from Bay City Roller (28-1), with Aidan O'Brien's 10-1 chance Diamond Necklace finishing third.

"To win this kind of race twice proves that Daryz is an exceptional horse," Barzalona told Sky Sports.

"It was a really tough race, it didn't go as we expected but he showed his talent and that made the difference in the end."

It was considered a gamble to keep last year's Arc winner in training aged four, when most top-class colts are retired at three because of the lucrative breeding fees.

But it has paid off for owners Aga Khan Studs, who claimed the winner's cheque of more than £2.5m.

Daryz added two further Group One victories to his tally this season and won his Arc prep race in grand style last month.

"He's a good horse, he's a champion," said jubilant winning trainer Graffard, following his second success in the race .

"It's rare that I am confident in the race - I always try to keep my feet on the ground because it is so hard to win these races.

"But I knew that if things were going right for him during the trip he was very hard to beat because he is a real champion."

articles.title: Eagles-Rams Week 4 prediction
articles.summary: ﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿﻿How are you feeling about this matchup?﻿﻿
articles.body:
Prior to last week's game between the Philadelphia Eagles and Chicago Bears, I wrote about how the onus was on Vic Fangio's defense to rise to the challenge. They did not.

This week, I feel like the onus is on Nick Sirianni. This isn't a must-win game for the Eagles. The Rams are a tough opponent and the Eagles are missing some key players (then again, so is LA).

It IS a must-compete game. The Eagles must put forth a better effort than we saw on Monday night. They can't look totally outcoached again.

This is a rare instance where it feels like a moral loss is an acceptable outcome. I'm not saying it'll feel great. Losing sucks. But this team hasn't played a very inspiring brand of football for most of this season. It would be encouraging to see improvement, even if it doesn't result in a win.

If the Eagles look out of sorts coming off an embarrassing loss and Sirianni can't get the team ready to play, well, what are we doing here?

Score prediction: 28 to 24, Eagles lose.

articles.title: Patriots Week 4 injury report vs. Bills: What it means for fantasy football
articles.summary: Drake Maye practiced fully throughout the week, but offensive support concerns and defensive absences complicate New England’s fantasy outlook against Buffa...
articles.body:
Drake Maye practiced fully throughout the week, but offensive support concerns and defensive absences complicate New England's fantasy outlook against Buffalo.

The New England Patriots enter Week 4 with encouraging news at quarterback and more uncertainty elsewhere. Drake Maye carries no game designation despite appearing on the supplied injury report with a right shoulder issue.

Christian Barmore , Christian Gonzalez , Channing Canada and Brenden Schooler are ruled out. Six other players are questionable, including offensive tackle Morgan Moses, fullback Reggie Gilliam and tight end Eli Raridon. Fantasy managers must separate Maye's availability from the surrounding personnel concerns.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Maye's practice week provides reassurance

Maye participated fully Wednesday, Thursday and Friday. That consistent involvement, combined with the absence of a questionable, doubtful or out designation, provides no injury basis for removing him from fantasy consideration.

Managers already planning to start Maye can retain that approach without treating his shoulder listing as an automatic downgrade. However, full participation does not guarantee unrestricted performance or establish how many passing attempts, rushing opportunities or touchdowns he will generate.

His fantasy value still depends on the matchup, expected offensive workload and alternatives available on your roster.

The same restraint applies to New England's receivers. Maye's practice status is reassuring for the passing offense, but it does not support inventing target projections or declaring every receiving option a strong start.

Moses missed Wednesday and Thursday with a foot injury before returning for limited participation Friday. He remains questionable, leaving an offensive tackle availability question unresolved.

His return represents progress rather than confirmation that he can handle his usual responsibilities. If Moses cannot play, the Patriots would need another blocking arrangement, potentially affecting protection and the time available for passing plays to develop.

That possibility merits attention when evaluating Maye, but it is not enough by itself to recommend benching him. Offensive line uncertainty should influence close lineup decisions, not override established player value without evidence.

Gilliam's knee injury produced limited participation Wednesday, an absence Thursday and another limited session Friday. His questionable status matters primarily through blocking and personnel flexibility rather than fantasy scoring.

Managers should avoid assuming that his absence would automatically create additional carries for a specific running back. Different formations can redistribute blocking assignments without changing the rushing workload.

Also, Raridon was limited throughout the practice week with a thigh injury and remains questionable. Managers considering him in deeper leagues should have an alternative ready rather than interpret three limited sessions as confirmation of availability.

Even if active, the report does not establish his expected routes, targets or snap share. A healthy alternative with a clearer receiving role may offer a more dependable option.

Official inactive lists arrive approximately 90 minutes before kickoff. Check that announcement for Raridon, Moses and Gilliam before finalizing lineup decisions.

Barmore and Gonzalez missed all three practices with shoulder injuries and are out . Canada is also out with a hamstring injury; the supplied report shows two limited sessions without a complete Friday entry.

articles.title: Is Jalen Coker playing today? Panthers injury update for Week 4
articles.summary: The latest on Panthers wide receiver Jalen Coker.
articles.body:
Carolina Panthers wide receiver Jalen Coker was listed as questionable on the team's final Week 4 injury report with the quadriceps injury he suffered last Sunday. However, after missing the entire second half of the team's loss to the Browns , he doesn't appear ready to return to the lineup just yet.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Sunday morning Coker is unlikely to play in the team's prime-time game against the Detroit Lions . It's unfortunate considering how beatable the Lions secondary has been this year, as they rank 28th in fantasy football points allowed to wide receivers this year.

Xavier Legette is also out for the Panthers with a knee injury.

Coker fantasy managers should prepare to start another player with the Panthers receiver likely out. It's unfortunate, as this would have been a terrific matchup, but those desperate for a replacement can still consider his teammate, Brycen Tremayne. The ex-Stanford receiver made the most of his playtime last week, making four catches for 83 yards.

articles.title: Penguins/Canadiens Highlights: Overtime win
articles.summary: The Penguins built a 5-1 lead last night in their home opener against Montreal, which they squandered away but managed to win the game in overtime. Here’s th...
articles.body:
The Penguins built a 5-1 lead last night in their home opener against Montreal, which they squandered away but managed to win the game in overtime.

"I think the fact that we found a way to get the extra point in overtime, especially with those last couple of minutes, you're not going into overtime with the best feeling," Head Coach Dan Muse said. "But they stuck with it. We found a way. We got the two points. We got plenty that we can look at now that we know we got to fix, and I'm confident that this group will work to correct those things."

There's certainly a lot to correct after a night that featured a lot of similarities to many a game last year where the Pens would blow multi-goal third period leads. Last season that often ended up in a shootout loss, Tommy Novak was able to prevent that by scoring in overtime.

Ben Kindel and Andrei Kuzmenko made their season debuts last night. Kindel scored a power play goal. Elmer Soderblom and Ville Koivunen came out of the lineup to make way for the new players.

"I think any game you're going to have things that you are going to look back on," Muse said. "Even at Philly, like, you're going to look back, there's still things to clean up. There's more things to clean up after tonight, for sure."

"Even throughout the game, with the chances that we're giving up there, some breakaways – Arty had to make some massive saves, especially early in the game. We got to clean it up. And so, that's something that we went into this year knowing that we have to."

There will be plenty of chances upcoming to clean those issues up, the Penguins play four times in the next week, starting with a game tomorrow night at home against Winnipeg.

articles.title: The Daily: Insider Says Edvinsson Wants Out; Red Wings Need to Find Scoresheet

articles.body:
One would think the Red Wings moved their base of operations 61 miles northwest to Hell (Michigan) based on the news fans have received to start the season.

Dylan Larkin is still here, and injured, but wants out.

Marco Kasper is injured after being the most electric part of the Red Wings first game.

And now, according to Sportsnet Insider Elliotte Friedman, Simon Edvinsson, who went back to Sweden after not getting a new contract after Red Wings training camp, is now looking to book a return flight somewhere other than Detroit.

Friedman did qualify the information from the report by saying that neither the Red Wings or Edvinsson's agent were speaking on the matter. However, the sense he was getting from other teams around the league was that the big bodied Swedish blueliner has grown frustrated with Detroit.

Detroit for the moment is filling in his spot with the smallest of their remaining Swedish defenseman, Albert Johansson. However, losing the big Swede would be another blow to a Detroit team that simply cannot afford to lose his production.

The Red Wings were shut out in their home opener, and while their head coach is hoping that a heavier, more aggressive checking game will help them get in the o-zone, they'll still need help getting pucks on net. Losing a 25+ point shutdown pairing defenseman is a good way to find your team playing on their back foot on a night to night basis.

Todd McLellan knows you've got to make the best of the hand you're dealt.

articles.title: Seike double helps Brighton to first WSL win of season
articles.summary: Kiko Seike scores twice as Brighton recover from conceding an early goal to defeat Charlton and secure their first win of the season in the Women's Super Lea...
articles.body:
Brighton & Hove Albion 5 - 1 Charlton Athletic FT

Kiko Seike scored twice as Brighton defeated Charlton to secure their first win of the season in the Women's Super League.

Charlton, who won promotion from the Championship last season, had only scored once in their opening four league games, losing all of them.

However, the visitors took a third-minute lead when Cassandra Korhonen reacted quickest to score the rebound after her first attempt had been saved by home goalkeeper Chiamaka Nnadozie.

But the Seagulls quickly took control of the game and scored a 26th-minute equaliser when Olivia Garcia got to the byline and pulled the ball back for Seike to score.

Brighton took the lead just before half time with a similar goal to their first. Garcia was again the provider, with former England international Fran Kirby applying the finish.

Any hope of a Charlton fightback ended in the 54th minute when Seike grabbed her second of the afternoon, firing a loose ball home from inside the penalty area.

Brighton scored again late on when Maisie Symonds got a slight touch on Marisa Olislagers' right-wing corner and Gabby George made it 5-1, heading in from close range deep into added on time.

Charlton remain the only WSL side to have zero points, with five losses from their opening five games.

They are also only the third team in WSL history to be beaten in all of their first five matches. Yeovil Town lost seven in a row in 2017 and Leicester City began the 2021-22 campaign with nine successive defeats.

articles.title: WATCH: Commanders' Rasul Douglas picks off Daniel Jones for second takeaway of game
articles.summary: Commanders safety Rasul Douglas got his first interception since joining Washington in their game against the Indianapolis Colts in London.
articles.body:
It is only the second quarter, but the Washington Commanders already have two takeaways in their game against the Indianapolis Colts , including an interception by safety Rasul Douglas. Washington had a strip sack against Colts quarterback Daniel Jones in the first quarter.

Here is a look at the interception, courtesy of the Washington Commanders' official social media:

This was Douglas' first interception with the Commanders, as his role has increased with Mike Sainristil playing fewer snaps. Douglas played 49 percent of the defensive snaps in the Commanders' first three games. Washington now has at least two turnovers in their last two games after not generating a takeaway in their first two games.

The Commanders couldn't capitalize on Douglas' interception after failing to convert on fourth down near midfield. Washington's defense looked like they were going to get off the field and force a field goal attempt, but a 15-yard penalty against Commanders cornerback Amik Robertson extended the drive for Indianapolis. The Colts capitalized with a touchdown to take the lead shortly before halftime.

Indianapolis kicked a field goal just before halftime and went into intermission with a 10-6 lead.

articles.title: Evans claims dramatic WRC title after Solberg crash
articles.summary: Five-time runner-up Elfyn Evans is world champion for the first time after rival Oliver Solberg crashes in the final moments of Rally Italia Sardegna.
articles.body:
Five-time runner-up Elfyn Evans is world champion for the first time after rival Oliver Solberg crashed in a dramatic finish to the Rally Italia Sardegna.

Sweden's Solberg was on course to snatch the lead on the final stage of the last round of the World Rally Championship (WRC) when he crashed with less than 100 metres to go.

"It hasn't sunk in," said a shocked Evans, who became the first British world champion in 25 years.

"I was sure it was over. I feel for Oliver, he had an incredible weekend. I don't know what to say."

The 37-year-old and co-driver Scott Martin had led for much of the 2026 season and took a 21-point advantage into the final round in Sardinia.

But that gap had shrunk to a solitary point by the time the drivers lined up for the last of 17 stages, bringing back painful memories of previous narrow misses for Evans.

Solberg, 25, needed only to beat his Toyota team-mate in the final stage to claim enough bonuses to be champion, but crashed two corners from the finish.

Evans becomes only the third British man to win the WRC title after Colin McRae in 1995 and Richard Burns in 2001.

Solberg, whose father Petter won the WRC title in 2003, won the rally by almost a minute ahead of nine-time world champion Sebastien Ogier.

He and English co-driver Elliott Edmondson were also on course to win the final stage and collect a maximum 35 points for the weekend to take the title by two points.

However, his crash meant he finished five points behind Evans in the overall standings.

A third Toyota driver, Sami Pajari, finished a further one point behind in third - having seen his own title challenge evaporate on the final weekend.

An inconsolable Solberg remained in his car for some time at the end of the stage before being encouraged to take to the podium by Gazoo Racing team principal Jari-Matti Latvala and team-mate Ogier.

"Two corners, two corners," said an emotional Solberg.

"First congratulations to Elfyn, he has been very consistent all season. That I even had a shot after my rollercoaster of a season is incredible.

"I tried everything. I knew I was pushing but didn't know if it was enough. I pushed even more and I couldn't save the car. I tried my very best."

Evans, from Dolgellau in north Wales, had previously missed out on the title on the final day three times and in two of those seasons he had taken a lead into the concluding rally before losing out to Ogier in 2020 and 2025.

"I don't really know what my reaction is. It's surreal with how it happened. It's a relief," he said.

"It wouldn't by my proudest way of winning it, but it's job done."

For Toyota sporting director Kaj Lindstrom there were mixed feelings.

"That was the hardest thing. The ending was quite something, I didn't expect it," said the Finn.

"It was a good fight and we all saw that Oliver was all or nothing. It held all the way to the end.

"Oliver still has time but Elfyn finally got his title so we're really happy for him."

The WRC season was reduced to 13 rounds when the Saudi Arabia event, originally planned for next month, was cancelled because of the ongoing unrest in the Middle East.

Rally Italia Sardegna marked the end of Jon Armstrong's rookie season at the top level of WRC, and he produced his best result when finishing seventh.

"It's been good to have a clean weekend with a strong result," said the M-Sport Ford driver.

"It's not been an easy year and this was a rally to show we can put it together. A big thanks to everyone who has been supporting us, it's been a great year and it's been a privilege to drive this car."

Armstrong's team-mate and fellow Irishman Josh McErlean did not fare as well despite running as high as sixth on Saturday before retiring after a collision with a tree.

He also had to stop twice on Sunday before finishing well off the pace but claimed ninth spot in the championship.
